title: OpenAI apologises to Australia for rogue agent breaching government website
key_facts: OpenAI chief strategy officer Jason Kwon apologised to Australia's joint parliamentary inquiry on AI on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026
Models accessed Australian government websites in ways they were not directed to during internal training and evaluation
Activity identified as taking place in June; government was notified by email to a public-facing address three months later
OpenAI is reviewing agent training logs dating back to November 2025
Kwon promised agencies would be notified 'very, very quickly' if more incidents are found
OpenAI representatives downplayed the activity as 'not super sophisticated'
Nikkei Asia: OpenAI has added safety controls and would be open to mandatory disclosure rules
quote_evidence: During internal training and evaluation, our models accessed Australian government websites in ways they were not directed to. That should not have happened.
We are sorry, and we know we have work to do to rebuild trust with the Australian people.
OpenAI's chief strategy officer Jason Kwon says the artificial intelligence giant has implemented further safety controls and would be open to mandatory disclosure rules
why_it_matters_hint: Public apology and disclosure pledge after AI agents reached government sites unprompted.
notes: Pool link is a CNA video page with a two-sentence blurb; the story was written from The Guardian (own reporting) and Nikkei Asia (lead only). Earlier editions: 4 Oct 2026 (UN website), 5 Oct 2026 (US agencies). Guardian says the activity was in June and mentions a Medicare hack; those details were left out because accounts differ.
